findings.reason: the honest change is one new method (`comment_on_pull_request`) on `_GitHubClient`, which the plan already identified; leaving it forked drifts the two boundaries and lets the next refusal/receipt writer choose a third.
findings.text: the plan introduces `_pull_request_comment` (POST `/repos/{repo}/issues/{number}/comments`) and `_pull_request_call` (:1459 GET) as a fresh PR REST boundary, re-implementing the transport that `imas_codex/standard_names/catalog_release.py:58` `_GitHubClient) already owns and self-describes as "the single pull-request boundary; every call goes over GitHub REST" (create_pull_request :75, update_pull_request_body :104, read_pull_request_body :115); the plan's own followup (f-crs-the-refusal-reaches-the-request-itself) named that owner as the reusable transport, yet the landed path forked it. The same parallel-boundary type recurs at imas_codex/standard_names/promote.py:2013-2022 (comment/review reads through `_pull_request_call`) and, pre-existing, at imas_codex/standard_names/review_triage.py:160, so the census is three direct `github_api_call` PR boundaries beside the one declared owner.

findings.reason: the plan should say "extend `_GitHubClient`" or give a reason a parallel boundary is required; as written it prescribes a second API surface over the same machinery.
findings.text: `_pull_request_comment` adds no behaviour `_GitHubClient` could not carry; it is a three-line forwarder to `github_api_call` POST, and the plan text says only that "the transport beneath it exists and is reusable" without stating why the owner cannot be extended.

findings.reason: the section must account for the added interface surface in its own text, e.g. by folding the refusal notice through `_GitHubClient` rather than adding a second public refusal entry point.
findings.text: §4's deliverable-three design adds the public definitions `notify_refusal_on_pull_request` and `refusal_notice_body` (:1491) and a new refusal surface on the reviewer's request, against a supplied budget of 0 public_definitions and 0 refusal_families, and the section names nothing it retires or merges nor why nothing can be.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — no new module is proposed; the whole plan wires existing machinery (mark_catalog_name_approved, undo_approval, github_api_call) behind the existing entry points, so there is no new interface to weigh against hidden behaviour.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan adds a second pull-request REST boundary in promote.py beside catalog_release.py's _GitHubClient, which declares itself "the single pull-request boundary".
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §4's deliverable three adds the public functions notify_refusal_on_pull_request and refusal_notice_body and a new refusal surface without naming anything it retires or merges, or stating why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan carries a reuse map (17 candidates, 17 verdicted) and a prior-art scout (44/44 citations verified) naming the traceability writer, the unwind path and the temp-neo4j substrate; the residual gap it names (the reviewer-visible refusal) is a real missing call site, not an unsearched subsystem. Line anchors have drifted since (mark_catalog_name_approved is at promote.py:1723, not :1627; undo_approval at :1645, not :1549) but every row names the symbol so it stays findable.
